$comment: SCHEMA EXAMPLE written in Phase 0. Status 'draft' — it does not count toward mastery and is excluded from builds until reviewed and approved in Phase 3. Numbers are generated from parameters; the reference answer is computed by the named solver, never typed by hand or by AI.
$constraintsNote: The block must stay at rest (so the answer is the static friction actually needed, mg sin θ, not μs N), with a margin so rounding never flips the case.
stem: A {{m}} kg block rests on a rough plank tilted at {{theta}}°. The coefficient of static friction is {{mu_s}}. Take g = 9.8 m/s². What is the magnitude of the friction force acting on the block?

hints.text: Is the block moving? What does that tell you about the net force along the plank?
Turn on tilted axes. Which forces have a component along the plank?
Along the plank, friction must exactly balance mg sin θ. μs N is only the most friction could be.

static-friction-always-max.text: You found the maximum static friction, μs N. The block isn't slipping, so friction is only as large as it needs to be.

normal-equals-weight.text: On an incline the plank pushes back only against the part of the weight pressing into it.

sin-cos-swap-incline.text: Check which component points along the plank. The angle between the weight and the plank's normal is θ.

dimension-mismatch.text: Friction is a force. Check your units.

generic.text: Compare the forces along the plank. What has to balance for the block to stay still?

workedSolution.text: The block is at rest, so the net force along the plank is zero.
Resolve the weight: mg sin θ = {{m}} × 9.8 × sin {{theta}}° acts down the plank.
Static friction acts up the plank and balances it: f = mg sin θ = {{answer}}.
Check: the maximum available is μs mg cos θ = {{maxStatic}}, which is larger, so the block indeed stays at rest.

accessibility.altText: Block on a plank tilted at {{theta}} degrees, with its weight drawn straight down.
accessibility.nonDragAlternative: Forces can be added from a menu and set with angle and magnitude inputs.
